apis.Name: sap_service_ticketing_recommendation_api
apis.Title: Solution Recommendation - Service Ticket Intelligence
apis.ShortText: Based on historical resolved requests, this API recommends similar solutions for new incoming tickets.
apis.Description:
Service Ticket Intelligence helps to build a self-driven customer service powered by machine learning. Based on historical resolved requests, Service Ticket Intelligence proposes similar questions and recommended answers. 

Incoming customers service tickets are automatically classified (refer to Text Classification - Service Ticket Intelligence) into their categories, and routed to the right agent. The agent is then provided with recommended solutions to improve operational efficiency. 

Service Ticket Intelligence leverages deep learning neural networks trained on large amounts of historical data. The model understands the semantics of unstructured ticket messages, classifies the ticket into their most likely categories and recommends solutions or knowledge base articles from similar previously answered tickets for the agent. With more processed service tickets and users' feedback the model improves over time.

apis.Name: sap_service_ticketing_classification_api
apis.Title: Text Classification - Service Ticket Intelligence
apis.ShortText: Based on historical service tickets, this API predicts the categories of new incoming service tickets.
apis.Description:
Service Ticket Intelligence helps to build a self-driven customer service powered by machine learning. Based on historical service tickets that have been classified into different categories, Service Ticket Intelligence predicts the categories of new incoming service tickets. 

Incoming customers service tickets are automatically classified into their categories, and routed to the right agent. The agent is then provided with recommended solutions (refer to Solution Recommendation - Service Ticket Intelligence) to improve operational efficiency. 

Service Ticket Intelligence leverages deep learning neural networks trained on large amounts of historical data. The model understands the semantics of unstructured ticket messages, classifies the ticket into their most likely categories and recommends solutions or knowledge base articles from similar previously answered tickets for the agent. With more processed service tickets and users' feedback the model improves over time.

apis.Name: cf_producer_api
apis.Title: Cloud Foundry Producer
apis.ShortText: Allows posting custom events that can be consumed in a system of choice defined in your subscriptions.
apis.Description:
Use the Alert Notification Producer API as a means to post custom events regarding your application. Those events could be the reflection of important to the business and operations things that happen within the application.

In Alert Notification, events are divided in three categories:
* Alert
* Notification
* Exception

In addition, severity and priority can be adjusted according to your needs. Take a look in the model tab of the post request where all possible properties for the event description are listed. Alert Notification gives you the option to extend those properties if needed by adding your own tags in the tags object at the end.

apis.Description:
Welcome to the Incentive Management REST API reference. This page documents the REST resources available in Incentive Management results entities (SalesOrder, SalesTransaction, Deposit, Incentive, Payment etc, along with expected HTTP response codes and sample requests.

  Incentive Management REST API can be used to build add-ons for Incentive Management, develop integrations between Incentive Management and other applications, or script interactions with Incentive Management. All REST operations require authentication credentials for an active Incentive Management user and perform the operation in the role of that user. The current API version is v2. The REST API uses JSON as its communication format, and the standard HTTP methods like GET, PUT, POST and DELETE.





      GET :
          The GET endpoints retrieve a single resource or list of resources.
          By default this will return all the resources. For version resources, we can apply startDate and endDate to retrieve the resource with
          specific date range. This endpoint supports other features like pagination, sorting, partial response ('select') and related fields ('expand').

      POST:
          The POST endpoint is used to create resource.
          We need to pass list of objects with required and/or additional (optional) properties.
          For reference properties, we need to pass as object contains either primary value (unique id)
          or list of logical properties.

      PUT:
          The PUT endpoint is used to update resource. We can pass list of objects with either primay property or list of logical properties 
          and the additional properties to update. For reference properties,
          we can pass as object contains either primary value (unique id) or list of logical properties.

      DELETE:
          The DELETE endpoint delete the resource. To delete multiple resources, pass list of unique ids as string separated by comma.

  **Response Codes** :

      Across all services some standard codes are used which are detailed in the table below.

        Code      Status                  Description

        200       OK                      Successful operation
        201       Created                 New resource has been created successfully
        204       No Content              Operation was successful, but no data has been returned
        207       Multi-Status            Bulk operation was partially successful. Body has details
        304       Not Modified            Operation was successful, but no data has been modified
        400       Bad Request             There was an error in the request
        401       Unauthorized            User is not authorized to perform the request
        403       Forbidden               User is not authorized to perform the request
        404       Not Found               Requested URI does not match a Commissions endpoint
        412       Precondition Failed     ETag does not match. User is attempting to PUT stale data
        500       Internal Server Error   Unexpected error on the Commissions server

  **Pagination** :

      Some calls listed here support pagination, which are detailed in the individual sections listed here. Where pagination is available,
      the following fields are used:

        Parameter      Default Value    Description

        skip           0                The subset of N elements skip from the Collection and selecting only the remaining elements (starting with Entry N+1)
        top            10               The first N number of element in the collection, where N is an integer greater than or equal to zero.
                                        The maximum allowed is 100
        inlineCount    false            The query option specifies that the response to the request includes a count of the number of elements.
                                        Values allowed: true or false

      For example:
        https://{domain-name}/{serviceName}/tcmp/rest/v2/positions?skip=15&top=5
        Return results from 16 to 20

      When pagination is included in a call the pagination object is included as below. 
      Prev and next are only included if there are previous or next results available.
      Total is the total number of elements available in the results.

       {
         ...
         "prev": "/v2/positions?skip=1&top=1",
         "next": "/v2/positions?skip=3&top=1",
         "total": 2342
       }
  **Filtering** :

      Filtering is determined through the use of the '$filter' query string parameter. The value of this parameter is a expression contains single or
  multiple condition. The expression can be defined as,

      - expression := [(] expression [)] | not expression | expression (and | or) expression | simple-expression
          - The order of precedence is: (), not, and, or
      - simple-expression := field op value
      - field := property | property/field (property - the property name of an object)
      - property := the property name of an object
      - op := as Operator (listed below table),
         - For like operations, use
             eq or ne with the wildcard * in the string, such as abc*, *abc, *abc*, a*bc
      - value := null | literal | 'literal' | "literal"
        - null value is valid for operators, eq and ne.
        - 'literal' or "literal" is required to accept special characters like (, ), space, and/or operators, etc.
             Ex: 'this is an example', 'a or b', '(abc)', '1/1/2018 12:30'
        - To escape quotes in a quoted literal
             For 'literal', to escape a single quote, use two single quotes.
                 Ex: 'a''bc' is a'bc
        - For "literal", to escape a double quote, use two double quotes.
             Ex: "a""bc" is a"bc
        - To pass value with unit type - pass both number and name of unitType in single/double quotes separated by space.
             Ex: '100000 USD', '10 Percent'

      Logical Operators :

        Operator   Description

        eq         matches exactly (default)
        ne         not equal to
        gt         greater than
        ge         greater than or equal
        lt         less than
        le          less than or equal

      Other Operators :

        Operator   Description

        ()         Precedence grouping
        null       Supported by eq and ne operator.
        like       Supported by eq and ne operator with the wildcard *.

  **Sorting**:

      Sorting is determined through the use of the 'orderBy' query string para meter. The value of this parameter is a comma-separated list of sort keys.
      Sort direction can optionally be appended to each sort key, using the 'asc' and 'desc' character. Defaulty sort order is ascending.

      For example:
        https://{domain-name}/{serviceName}/tcmp/rest/v2/participants?orderBy=lastName,hireDate desc
        Get list of Participant sorted by last name in ascending and hire date in descending order.

  **Related Fields**:

      By default the GET end point will return the ID (seq) of related resources. For example, the position resource returns the ID for title,
      payee, manager, and processingUnit. The underlying lightweight bean has the ability to look up details for related resources.
      The v2 API will provide optional lookup of related fields by using the following parameter:

        Parameter  Value

        expand     {field1},{field2}

  **Partial Response** :

      By default the GET endpoints will return all the information of related resources. If we want to GET only specific information
       of resources then the v2 API will provide option to specify the selected fields by using the following parameter:

        Parameter  Value

        select     {field1},{field2}

  **Versioning** (only support single resource per API) :

      The Commission Rest APIs also support the versioning for effective dated resources, by appending the '/versions' at end of URI Path.
      The version APIs handle only single resource at a time, and support create, update and delete operation on that resource.
       https://{domain-name}/{serviceName}/tcmp/rest/v2/{resource-name}(:{resource-id})/versions

        GET: The GET endpoints retrieve all the versions for the single resource. This endpoint is also support partial response ('select')
        and related fields ('expand'). We can filter the versions for specific date range by providing the startDate and endDate as query parameter.

        POST: The POST endpoints delete all existing versions and create new ones as per request payload.
        If we are updating version within entire range of resource, then we can use PUT, and pass payload for version to update or create.
        The POST endpoint is useful when we are changing entire range of existing record.

        PUT: The PUT endpoints only update the versions which are passed in payload.
        We can also modify existing versions by creating multiple versions from single, or combining the multiple versions into single version.
        This endpoint will not change entire effective range of resource.

        DELETE: The DELETE endpoints delete all the versions valid for given date range (query params - startDate and endDate),
        by extending the previous or next versions. This operation does not impact the entire range of the resource.
        We can also specify how to fill the gaps (from previous or next, only if we delete middle versions) by providing the flag 'fillFromRight',
        or it will always fill gap by previous version.

  **Note**:

      1. In a Json payload, attributes which are empty or null values will be processed and  set. How ever, there are two exceptions.

        - on a create null values will be ignored.
        - on an update, if an empty or null is set for an attribute which has default value it will error out.

      2. For VariableAssignment resource, we do not support the POST or PUT operation directly. However, we can update the VariableAssignment as part of updating the resources like Position.

                  Examle:       https://{domain-name}/{serviceName}/tcmp/rest/v2/positions

                    Request Type: PUT

                    Payload: [
                                    {
                                      "ruleElementOwnerSeq": "4785074605532228",
                                          "effectiveStartDate": "1/1/2015",
                                          "effectiveEndDate": "1/1/2200",
                                          "variableAssignments": [
                                            {
                                              "owner": {
                                                "ruleElementOwnerSeq": "4785074605532228",
                                                "effectiveStartDate": "1/1/2015",
                                                "effectiveEndDate": "1/1/2200"
                                              },
                                              "variable": {
                                                "ruleElementSeq": "19703248372468492",
                                                "effectiveStartDate": "1/1/2015",
                                                "effectiveEndDate": "1/1/2200"
                                              },
                                              "assignment": {
                                                "ruleElementSeq": "19421773395757800"
                                              }
                                            }
                                          ]
                                    }
                              ]

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ContrAcctgBillingRequest-v1
apis.Title: Contract Accounting Billing Request
apis.ShortText: Data Product Contract Accounting Billing Request
apis.Description: A contract accounting billing request is an object containing the information required by Convergent Invoicing to correct an existing invoicing document. A contract accounting billing request is used if an invoicing document is to be corrected but not reversed. The correction can be made in the form of a credit memo or debit memo.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ContrAcctgDocument-v1
apis.Title: Contract Accounting Document
apis.ShortText: Data Product Contract Accounting Document
apis.Description:
A contract accounting document (FI-CA document) is a document in the Contract Accounting sub-ledger.
Contract accounting documents consist of header data, business partner items and general ledger items.
In addition to the unique document number, the header data also contains the document type as the classifying attribute, the currency key and various date specifications.
All items contain the posting amount and the necessary information for General Ledger Accounting, Cash Management and Controlling.
The items in contract accounts also contain specifications regarding the due date, cash discount, for controlling dunning, automatic payments or debit memos as well as for calculating interest.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ContrAcctgInvoicingDocument-v1
apis.Title: Contract Accounting Invoicing Document
apis.ShortText: Data Product Contract Accounting Invoicing Document
apis.Description: A contract accounting invoicing document is a commercial document issued to a customer, containing details of a receivable or credit. An invoicing document is used as a statement to justify a receivable for a provided service, notify the receiver about a certain credit, or inform the receiver about unpaid invoices, interests, or dunning fees. An invoicing document contains information about the amount due, payment terms, provided service, taxation, and in some countries special information assigned by public authorities, such as official document numbers.

apis.ShortText: Data Product Contract Accounting Billing Plan
apis.Description: A contract accounting billing plan is an object containing the information required to schedule payments in Convergent Invoicing. A billing plan defines when and how often an amount is invoiced to a customer.

apis.Description: A contract accounting billing document is a document created by the data transfer process, containing the information required by invoicing in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable. The information in this billing document is used to bill services performed for a customer.

apis.Name: Mobile
apis.Title: Mobile Service
apis.ShortText: Provides basic methods for mobile application handling.
apis.Description: Basic Methods for the Mobile Environment. This is a specialized service designed for mobile ticketing applications that enables customers to manage their event tickets directly on their mobile devices. It provides endpoints for mobile-specific workflows including customer login authentication, retrieving purchased tickets for download either by invoice or all recent tickets from the last three months, listing ticket IDs only, fetching individual ticket data, confirming successful ticket receipt which marks tickets as printed and optionally stores NFC/RFID smartphone UIDs, and forwarding tickets to other customers via mobile number with format validation. The service supports online shop sessions, includes comprehensive error handling with history tracking for login events, and automatically resets ticket download status to allow repeated retrieval until confirmation.

apis.Name: Infodelivery
apis.Title: Infodelivery Service
apis.ShortText: Provides methods for the systematic export of business data, which enables external systems to query data in a structured way
apis.Description: Generate Basis Objects for Basic Setup. It is a comprehensive service for creating and managing the foundational master data and configuration objects in the SAP Event Ticketing system. It provides endpoints for setting up and maintaining the core ticketing infrastructure, including events, venues (houses), block templates (seating sections), price lists, pricing structures, performances, fee groups and charges, seat locking mechanisms, entry points, seat/row aliases, additional currencies, and product variants. The service supports both creation and update operations (upsert pattern), includes specialized functions like seat price assignment, invoice email sending, customer doublet merging, and synchronization requests, with all operations requiring session authentication and extensive validation through dedicated models, while maintaining history tracking for modified entities.

apis.Name: Order
apis.Title: Order Service
apis.ShortText: Provides methods for basic order, invoice, reservation and basket management.
apis.Description: Basket and booking management. This is the most comprehensive service  in the SAP Event Ticketing system, serving as the central hub for basket management, ticket reservation, ordering, and invoice operations. It provides  endpoints covering the complete order lifecycle including ticket reservation methods, basket operations, payment processing, invoice management , reservation/option handling, ticket operations , shipment configuration, chunk/time-slot ticket support, insurance confirmation, and specialized features for subscriptions, bundles, and group bookings. The service integrates history tracking, data validation, and extensive error handling with detailed return codes.

apis.Name: ExternalDocuments
apis.Title: External Documents
apis.ShortText: Exchanges electronic documents between your business system and external systems

apis.Name: Export
apis.Title: Export Service
apis.ShortText: Provides methods for the systematic export of business data, which enables external systems to query data in a structured way
apis.Description: Export of business data. The service is designed for the systematic export of business data from the SAP Event Ticketing system to external systems. It provides endpoints that follow a consistent list-get-tag pattern for exporting different entity types including invoices (with support for bundles and customer visibility filtering), customers, communication channels, addresses, customer group memberships, and merged customer records. The service uses a pull-based export mechanism where external systems first list available records by ID, retrieve individual or bundled records with complete data, and then tag them as exported to prevent re-export, with all operations requiring valid session authentication and supporting optional system identification for tracking export destinations.

apis.Name: Customer
apis.Title: Customer Service
apis.ShortText: Provides methods for basic customer data management and related data such as addresses, communication channels, or customer affiliations.
apis.Description: Basic customer data management. It is a comprehensive service for managing customer data and related entities in the SAP Event Ticketing system. It provides endpoints for complete customer lifecycle management, including creating, reading, updating, and merging customer records; managing customer addresses, communication channels (email, phone, etc.), and authorization credentials; handling customer groups and memberships; managing custom attributes and their values; controlling marketing consent preferences; and maintaining customer blocking lists. The service validates all inputs through dedicated validation models, requires valid session authentication for all operations, and integrates with legacy merchant system components while supporting features like address validation, duplicate detection, and GDPR-compliant data erasure.

apis.Name: Cache
apis.Title: Cache Service
apis.ShortText: Provides basic methods for cache management.
apis.Description: Basic cache management. The service provides endpoints for storing base64-encoded data with a specified TTL and for retrieving cached data by key, always with valid session authentication. The service enforces size limits (1MB) and expiration constraints on cache entries stored in a dedicated Redis database.

apis.Name: Advertising
apis.Title: Advertising Service
apis.ShortText: Provides basic methods for advertisement management.
apis.Description: Basic Advertisement management.

apis.Name: Session
apis.Title: Session Service
apis.ShortText: Provides methods for basic session management.
apis.Description: Session management and authentication. This is a service dedicated to comprehensive session lifecycle management and authentication for the SAP Event Ticketing system. It provides endpoints covering session initialization through multiple authentication methods, session validation and termination, session data management, customer login functionality for self-service access. The service supports both standard backend user sessions and online shop customer sessions, includes history tracking for login events, provides one-time token URL generation for secure access, and validates all operations through dedicated validation models.

apis.Name: InfoRequest
apis.Title: InfoRequest Service
apis.ShortText: Provides read-only methods for important business objects and data.
apis.Description: Management of important business objects and data. This is an extensive read-only service that provides comprehensive information retrieval capabilities for all major business objects and data in the SAP Event Ticketing system. It offers endpoints for querying events, performances, artists, venues (houses), price lists, prices, charges, fee groups, companies, SEPA data, performance categories, cities, blocks (seating sections), contingents, box office protocols, capacity data, ticket sales statistics, performance workload, accounting data, chunks, layout representations, reservation limits, performance pools, insurance claims, activation states, and change tracking. The service supports complex filtering options (by date ranges, company, event, performance status, categories), provides both simple and enhanced/matrix data formats for various entities, includes performance bookability checks and sales data aggregation, and requires session authentication for all operations and uses dedicated validation models.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudSalesData
apis.Title: Sales Data
apis.ShortText: This endpoint allows you to to have a direct, API-based connection to SAP Engagement Cloud where you can upload your sales data directly.
apis.Description:
With this endpoint you can send your sales data through a direct, API-based integration to SAP Engagement Cloud, without the need to create CSVs.
By using JSON objects with the Sales Data API, the process of uploading sales data became much easier then before.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudMediaDatabase
apis.Title: Media Database
apis.ShortText: Use these endpoints to manage your digital assets in the solution.
apis.Description:
The Media Database endpoints provide operations to create, list, retrieve, upload, and delete media files and folders. 
Use this API to programmatically manage digital assets within the SAP Engagment Cloud platform, enabling automation and integration with your marketing workflows.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudCorporateAccount
apis.Title: Corporate Account
apis.ShortText: The SAP Engagement Cloud Corporate Account API helps you to import Corporate Accounts and their related objects (relations, codelists) into SAP Engagement Cloud.
apis.Description: This API is used to create and update corporate account data and its related objects - (contact) relations and code lists. It supports extensible fields and code lists.

apis.Name: sap-bdc-sf-career-TalentProfile-v1
apis.Title: Data Product for Talent Profiles
apis.ShortText: Talent flag information of employees.
apis.Description: This data product enables you to access talent flag information of employees, such as Risk of Loss, Impact of Loss, and Reason for Leaving.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudCodeLists
apis.Title: Code Lists
apis.ShortText: The SAP Engagement Cloud Code List API allows retrieval of code lists and codes.
apis.Description:
This API provides endpoints to retrieve code lists and specific codes with optional language filtering. 
It is useful for developers needing to integrate code list data into applications, ensuring localized data retrieval and secure access.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudEmailCampaigns
apis.Title: Email Campaigns
apis.ShortText: Create and maintain email campaign data for your marketing needs.
apis.Description:
The Email Campaigns API enables you to programmatically create, manage, update, and retrieve email campaigns, including handling campaign versions, recipient sources, categories, languages, and blocklists.
You would use it to automate and integrate sophisticated email marketing workflows within your applications or systems, streamlining campaign management and personalization at scale.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudBulkResponseSummary
apis.Title: Bulk Response Summary
apis.ShortText: Email reporting related API endpoint. It is used to collect reporting information from multiple campaigns.
apis.Description: Use this endpoint to collect reporting information from multiple campaings, such as number of emails sent and received. You can also check email opens and clicks as well as different types of bounces to be able to determine your next steps in the email strategy.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudProductCatalog
apis.Title: Product Catalog
apis.ShortText: Manage product catalog items with localized information and availability.
apis.Description:
The Product Catalog API allows for the ingestion and updating of product catalog items, providing a structured way to manage localized product information and availability. 
This API is useful for businesses looking to efficiently update and maintain their product data across different locales, ensuring accurate and localized information is available to customers.

apis.Name: SAPEngagementCloudEngagementEvents
apis.Title: Engagement Events

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ServiceContract-v1
apis.Title: Service Contract
apis.ShortText: Data Product Service Contract
apis.Description: A service contract is a long-term agreement between a service provider and a customer, specifying the content and scope of services that are performed for the customer. A service contract describes which services will be performed for which objects and under which conditions. It consists of a header and one or more items. The header and each item can contain the following data: price agreement, validity period, texts, status, partner data, and so on. Each contract item can contain a service level agreement, billing plan, object list, product list, and so on.

apis.Name: API_SALES_ORDER_WITHOUT_CHARGE_SRV
apis.Title: Sales Order Without Charge (A2X)
apis.ShortText: Create, read, update, and delete sales orders without charge with this synchronous OData API
apis.Description:
In every API call, you can make use of the following operations:
 - You can read entire sales orders without charge or only parts of the data, using the provided filters.
 - You can create sales orders without charge. Note that you must use “deep insert” requests (a header plus the following entities: header partner, item and item partner). You cannot create entities without including any related entities.
 - For existing sales orders without charge, you can create new items. Note that you must use “deep insert” requests (with the entity: item partner). You cannot create entities without including any related entities.
 - For existing sales orders without charge, you can update the header, header partner, item and item partner.
 - For existing sales orders without charge, you can delete the header, header partner, item and item partner.

apis.Name: CDMSearchAPI
apis.Title: Core Data Search
apis.ShortText: Searching for the core data for a specific entity.
apis.Description: Core Data Search is an OData API based on the OpenAPI specification. This API provides a way for an application to search for core data in the Core data management Application. This API supports different search parameters. The payload must adhere to the One Domain Model (ODM) model.

apis.Name: InBoundAPI
apis.Title: Core Data Inbound Publishing
apis.ShortText: Enables replication of core data from source systems.
apis.Description: Core Data Inbound Publish is an OData API based on the OpenAPI specification. It provides a way for an external system to push core data changes, which can then be consumed by SAP Procurement applications through the Core Data Management application. This API supports a mix of created, updated, and deleted events, with a maximum payload size of 25,000 records, except for the BusinessPartner/Supplier entity, which is limited to 500 records. The payload must adhere to the One Domain Model (ODM) model

apis.Description: An environmental, health, and safety (EHS) location is a specific site or area within an organization that falls under the responsibility of the safety management team. Locations are structured logically to reflect their spatial or functional position within the company, aiding in incident management and data analysis.

apis.Title: Environment and Health and Safety Data Collection
apis.ShortText: Data Product Environment and Health and Safety Data Collection
apis.Description:
An environment, health, and safety (EHS) data collection is a collection of operational data for a specific EHS location. Each data collection has a defined frequency, unit of measurement, and subject. It is used to collect quantities of operational data to determine, calculate, or aggregate the environmental impact of facilities, such as the quantity of air emissions of a specific pollutant.

apis.Description:
A listed substance element is a listed substance, a listed substance variant, or a listed substance group. Listed substance elements are chemicals or substances (including certain compounds) that are described and regulated in the environmental authorities' official legislation.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-EHSLocationAggregation-v1
apis.Title: Environment and Health and Safety Location Aggregation
apis.ShortText: Data Product Environment and Health and Safety Location Aggregation
apis.Description:
An environment, health, and safety (EHS) location aggregation is an entity that enables you to aggregate emissions data for a particular location, for the purpose of reporting to environmental authorities and ensuring compliance with legislation. An aggregation consolidates data collected or calculated from individual sub-locations within the overall location structure, helping to provide a comprehensive view of environmental impact for efficient management and compliance assurance.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-EHSCalculationDefinition-v1
apis.Title: Environment and Health and Safety Calculation Definition
apis.ShortText: Data Product Environment and Health and Safety Calculation Definition
apis.Description:
An environment, health, and safety (EHS) calculation definition is a calculation of operational data for a specific EHS location. Each calculation definition has an equation, a frequency, a unit of measurement, and a subject. It is used to determine the environmental impact of facilities, for example, the amount of air emissions of a given pollutant.

Additionally, you can get information on the JMS resources available on the tenant as well as on those actually used by your integration flows.  
This API is implemented based on OData version 2 specification.

HTTP log files enables you to access technical system logs written during message processing on the runtime node. HTTP log files contain information on authentication and authorization errors for inbound HTTP communication. The trace log files contain processing information including message payload data.

apis.Name: SecurityContent
apis.Title: Security Content
apis.ShortText: Access and manage security content to configure secure connections with remote systems.
apis.Description:
Security content enables you to get, write or delete various security content. Depending on the kind of connection, the applied authorization and authentication options, and the direction of the request (either inbound or outbound), different kind of security content needs to be created and deployed on the tenant. You can manage the floowing security content types:
* User credentials
* OAuth2 client credentials
* Keystore entries
* Certificate-to-user mappings  
  
This API is implemented based on OData version 2 specification.
 If you like to request the OData API on your tenant, you need to know how to find out the address of the HTTP call. For more information, see [HTTP Calls and URL Components](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_INTEGRATION_SUITE/51ab953548be4459bfe8539ecaeee98d/ca75e12fc5904d96a038aef6c00db5fc.html).

apis.Name: CFAuditLogRetrievalAPI
apis.Title: Audit Log Retrieval API (Cloud Foundry environment)
apis.ShortText: Provides functionality to retrieve audit logs.
apis.Description: The audit log retrieval API V2 provides functionality for retrieving audit logs. The extraction of the audit logs is strictly limited to the records possessed by a tenant that is extracted from the XSUAA. The API supports server-side pagination with 5000 events per page. If the size of events is bigger than the server page size, the results are returned by the server on pages, providing the response header 'Paging' with the next page. The audit log retrieval API supports filtering the results based on time. If no time based filtering is specified, the results for the last 30 days are returned.

apis.Name: AuditlogSearchAPI
apis.Title: Audit Log Search
apis.ShortText: Search and retrieve NG audit logs with advanced filtering and multi-tenant support. Does not search Legacy logs.
apis.Description:
The Audit Log Search API enables secure, programmatic search and retrieval of audit logs from the NG data stream only. It supports advanced filtering by time, user, event type, and tenant source, and delivers results asynchronously via a single search ID for efficient handling of large datasets.

Note: This API version searches only the NG data stream. If your tenant also uses the Legacy data stream, use the V2 API version, which automatically searches both NG and Legacy streams in a single request for complete audit log coverage. Choose the API version that matches your specific use case.

apis.Name: AuditLogRetentionAPI
apis.Title: Audit Log Retention API (Neo environment)
apis.ShortText: Returns the active retention period for the audit logs or changes the active retention period.
apis.Description: The audit log retention API for Neo environment provides functionality for changing the audit logs retention period for an subaccount. It is a REST API that processes requests to retrieve the active retention period on the available audit log data, and allows the customer to change the active audit log retention period for their subaccount.

apis.Name: CFAuditLogWriteAPI
apis.Title: Audit Log Write API (Cloud Foundry environment)
apis.ShortText: Provides functionality to write audit logs.
apis.Description: The Audit Log Service provides an Audit Log Write REST API meant for SAP customers, which is responsible for the recording of audit relevant events for a given subaccount(tenant). The audit log records written via this Write API can afterwards be retrieved via the Audit Log Retrieval API (Cloud Foundry environment)

apis.Name: AuditLogRetrievalAPI
apis.Title: Audit Log Retrieval API (Neo environment)
apis.ShortText: Provides functionality to retrieve audit logs.
apis.Description: The audit log retrieval API provides functionality for retrieving audit logs. The rest API follows the OData 4.0 standard, providing the audit log results as OData with collection of JSON entities. The extraction of the audit logs is strictly limited to the records possessed by an account. The account is provided as part of the URL and compared to the account in the provided Authorization header OAuth token, that is being validated. The API supports both client and server side pagination. If the client requested page size is bigger than the server page size or undefined, the results are returned by the server on pages, providing the @odata.nextLink with the next result chunk in the OData response. If the client page size is smaller than the server one the client page size is used. The audit log retrieval API supports filtering the results based on time. The defined period should not extend 1 month per request. If no time based filtering is specified the results for the last 30 days are returned.

A work center is an area or section of a production facility where production operations are performed. Machines, Machine Group, Production line and People represent the work center that are used to perform the required production order operations.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ProductionOrderConfirmation-v1
apis.Title: Production Order Confirmation
apis.ShortText: Data Product Production Order Confirmation
apis.Description: A production order confirmation is a document that records the processing status of a production order, its operations, and sub-operations. Specifically, it documents the quantities of produced goods (yield and/or scrap), the quantity of produced goods to be reworked, the work center at which the operation was carried out, who performed the operations, the time spent, as well as the values for the work activities.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-ProductionVersion-v1

apis.ShortText: Data Product Production Version
apis.Description: A production version is a specific method or technique used to manufacture a particular material. It essentially combines a bill of material (BOM) and a production routing/master recipe to outline the production process. It determines which alternative BOM is used with which production routing/master recipe to produce or plan a material.

apis.Name: sap-s4com-EnterpriseResourceCapacity-v1
apis.Title: Enterprise Resource Capacity
apis.ShortText: Data Product Enterprise Resource Capacity
apis.Description:
An enterprise resource capacity is the ability to perform a particular task. Capacities are differentiated according to the following capacity types. 

* Pooled capacities
* Reference capacities
* Default capacities 

In manufacturing, capacity is denoted by machine or labor, and it is used for capacity planning to ensure that production resources are available to meet planned production demands, avoid overloads, and optimize capacity utilization.

apis.Name: GHGDataFormsAPIV1
apis.Title: GHG Data Forms
apis.ShortText: Maintain GHG data forms for business activities, waste generated in operations, meter readings, and energy bills.
apis.Description:
The GHG Data Forms API allows you to distribute the form-based data collection for the GHG data forms: - Business activities - Waste generated in operations - Meter readings - Energy bills ### Process Description First, you create a GHG data collection for a certain period in the [Manage GHG Data Collections](https://help.sap.com/docs/sustainability-footprint-management/application-help-for-corporate-and-products/using-manage-ghg-data-collections-application) app in the SAP Sustainability Footprint Management solution. Once the GHG data form generation is completed, you can retrieve and update the forms using the GHG Data Forms API.
This process description is based on GHG data forms for business activities. To retrieve and update other GHG data form types, replace `GHGDataFormsBusinessActivities` with the corresponding GHG data form type. 1. You can **retrieve the GHG data forms** based on the corresponding GHG data collection with the resource [`GHGDataCollections`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/get_GHGDataCollections). Use the query parameter `$expand=GHGDataFormsBusinessActivities`. 2. You can **retrieve the data from a GHG form** with the resource [`GHGDataFormsBusinessActivities`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/get_GHGDataFormsBusinessActivities_footprintInventoryScope___footprintInventoryScope___period___period___location___location___locationType___locationType___). Use the query parameter `$expand=Data`. 3. You can **update** the notes and the data of GHG data forms with the action [`massUpdate`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/post_GHGDataCollections_footprintInventoryScope___footprintInventoryScope___period___period____GHGDataFormsService_massUpdate). 4. Once the data collection is completed for a form, the status for this form can be **set to completed (`SC`)** with the action [`massUpdate`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/post_GHGDataCollections_footprintInventoryScope___footprintInventoryScope___period___period____GHGDataFormsService_massUpdate). It is also possible to set the status of a GHG data form to **not applicable (`NA`)** with the action [`massUpdate`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/post_GHGDataCollections_footprintInventoryScope___footprintInventoryScope___period___period____GHGDataFormsService_massUpdate). It is possible to **Reopen (`IP`)** a completed GHG data form with the action [`massUpdate`](https://api.sap.com/api/GHGDataFormsAPIV1/path/post_GHGDataCollections_footprintInventoryScope___footprintInventoryScope___period___period____GHGDataFormsService_massUpdate). Note that it is not possible to generate or regenerate GHG data forms using the GHG Data Forms API. This can be done in the Manage GHG Data Collections app in the SAP Sustainability Footprint Management solution. ### Getting Started Accessing the GHG Data Forms API is possible with the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow, with the scope `c21-ghg-data-forms-api`.
To try out the APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub, you must first configure an environment on SAP Business Accelerator Hub. #### Prerequisites To configure an environment, you need the ``, ``, `` and `` that you have obtained from your service key. For more information on how to create your service key, see [Creating Service Keys in Cloud Foundry](https://help.sap.com/viewer/09cc82baadc542a688176dce601398de/Cloud/en-US/6fcac08409db4b0f9ad55a6acd4d31c5.html).
The following example shows the service key information displayed in the Cloud Foundry environment: ```json { "endpoints": { "apihost": "/api" }, "uaa": { "clientid": "", "clientsecret": "", "url": "", ... }, ... } ``` #### Authentication Use the ``, ``, and `` to request an access token by sending a `POST` request to the *Token URL* endpoint `/oauth/token` with the Form URL encoded body: `grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=&client_secret=`.
The following example shows the expected *200 OK* response returned by this endpoint: ```json { "access_token": "", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": , "scope": "" } ``` To access the GHG Data Forms API, the space-delimited `` needs to contain the scope `.c21-ghg-data-forms-api`. #### Authorization The GHG Data Forms API endpoints are available at the URL `/api/ghgdata/v1/GHGDataFormsService`.
For sending requests to the GHG Data Forms API, pass the `` obtained above as HTTP `Authorization` header: ``` Authorization: Bearer ``` The updated GHG data forms will appear as "Changed By" the Client ID of your application. The Client ID will also appear in the Change History of the updated GHG data forms.
There is no instance-based permission model for the GHG Data Forms API. A client with the required scope can read and update all GHG data forms. ### Draft Handling The GHG Data Forms API allows modifications to GHG data forms even if other users are editing them. That happens in the following way: If an unsaved draft exists, the API responds to `massUpdate` requests for that specific GHG data form with a `409 Conflict` status. To override this draft protection and delete unsaved changes made by other users, you must include the header `X-Preserve-Changes: false` in your request. ### Mass Update Limits There are limits to the number of GHG data forms that you can update in a single request: - Maximum number of forms: 2000 - Maximum number of rows of data, across forms: 5000 ### Rate Limiting To ensure optimal performance and system stability, the API usage per tenant is limited as follows: - POST requests: 2 requests per second Best Practice: This API is designed for bulk operations. You should process multiple records in a single request rather than making separate calls for individual records. This will improve efficiency and reduce resource usage.

apis.Name: SfmMasterDataAPIV2
apis.Title: Import Master Data (Corporate and Products)
apis.ShortText: Imports master data for footprint calculations.
apis.Description:
# General

Receives the master data, from your source system and stores it in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management. The imported data is needed for footprint calculations, displaying the results, and performing analytics. Periodically aggregated transaction data is used as the basis for the calculations. The used aggregation is required, for example, per product, plant and (depending on the transaction type) other entities. These entities are referred to as master data. Master data entities are only imported with a human-readable identifier as a key. A technical key from the source system is not replicated to avoid additional mapping. The readable identifier is stored with a unique constraint.


 An import can include both new and pre-existing entries. The implementation checks if the human readable identifier already exists, and depending on whether it does, updates an existing entry or creates a new one. This means that the import is an `upsert`.


 Master data entities (and periodic data) may contain references to other master data entities (or custom units of measure). In cases where _referenced_ records have not yet been imported to the solution, data with invalid references is also accepted, however such _referenced_ records will be marked as inconsistent. In the case where a _referenced_ entity is imported, the consistency of the _referenced_ entity will be automatically re-calculated. The footprint calculation only considers consistent records.

## Lifecycle Actions
Master data can be created or updated continuously in the solution with Data Import Operations (see next section).

 Before pushing data, the source ERP needs to trigger a `notifyOfStartOfReplication`, create specific master data entities in packages and finally call `notifyOfEndOfReplication`. After the initial load, delta changes (creations and updates) can be pushed as well. This should be triggered automatically whenever ERP users change relevant data.

 The action `notifyOfStartOfReplication` sets the startReplication timestamp and the replication status, and deletes existing replication logs from previous runs. The body of the request must contain `{ masterDataTypeCode: <entity name> }`. Also, `All` is supported as an `<entity name>`.

  After all instances have been created in the solution, the action `notifyOfEndReplication` should be called, which sets the status in the solution to `Completed`. If a `ReplicationLog` with `logLevelCode = "E"` was created, the replication status will be set to the status `Aborted`. The body of the request must contain `{ masterDataTypeCode: <entity name> }`. To complete all entities at once, `All` is also supported as an `<entity name>`.

## Data Import Operations
The API to create and update master data is `massUpsert<entity>`. The body of the request must contain an array of entities to be created (or updated). Data with existing identifiers will be treated as updates and will NOT be rejected. This behavior supports the full load for the master data entities.


 Besides the master data entities itself, error logs can be created with the entity `ReplicationLog` with fields for the `masterDataTypeCode` (name of the entity, for example, Company), the `logLevelCode` and `messageText` (which can also be specified as a `Texts` array for different languages). Supported values for `logLevelCode` are I (info), W (warning), E (error), S (success). The ReplicationLog can also be created for `masterDataTypeCode = "All"`. This can be used to indicate errors in the initial load for all entities if the error cannot be attributed to a specific entity. In case the `notifyOfEndOfReplication` is called for `masterDataTypeCode = "All"` and the replication is not yet complete for some entities, the ReplicationLog entries for `masterDataTypeCode = "All"` will be added to the ReplicationLog for all remaining entities that are still in progress.

apis.Name: EmissionDataAPIV1
apis.Title: Import Emission Data (Corporate and Products)
apis.ShortText: Imports emission data for calculating footprints.
apis.Description: Replicates the emission data from your source system and stores it in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management. The replicated data is used to calculate footprints, displaying the results, and performing analytics. The operations have been grouped into logical categories and the following sections explain the important points about the operations. ## Lifecycle Actions To start the import of emission data, use the operation `notifyOfStartOfReplication`. Ensure that the body of the request contains `{ footprintInventoryScopeIdentifier: , period: "" }`. Mention the `period` in the ISO format (`yyyy` for a yearly aggregation or `yyyy-mm` for a monthly aggregation). This operation returns a `replicationId`, which identifies the combination of scope (periodicity and set of companies) and period, and is required as an input for all other actions. To restart the replication of the emission data for a specific replication ID, use the operation `notifyOfRestartOfReplication`. Ensure that the body of the request contains `{ replicationId: , emissionDataTypeCode: }`. This operation deletes all the previous records of emission data for the scope and period. After you start or restart a replication, you can import the actual data to the solution using the operations available under Data Import Operations. After the source system finishes replicating an emission data type, it calls `notifyOfEndOfReplication` to document the completion of the replication of this type. If you want to use this operation, ensure that the replication of all instances and log messages for an emission data type have been completed. Ensure that the body of the request contains `{ replicationId: , emissionDataTypeCode: }`. Sending the value `"All"` as an `entity name` completes in one call all the emission data types that are not yet completed. ## Data Import Operations Mass insert actions are available for importing the data. The emission data is only created once per period (usually after the period is closed and immutable). Hence, you can only _insert_ emission data and cannot send data twice for the same key. You can create error logs by using `massInsertReplicationLog`. The supported values for `logLevelCode` are I (info), W (warning), E (error), and S (success). You can also create the `ReplicationLog` for `emissionDataTypeCode = "All"`. You can use this to indicate errors across all the emission data types. If you create a `ReplicationLog` with `logLevelCode = "E"`, the replication ends with the status `Aborted`. If you call `notifyOfEndOfReplication` using `emissionDataTypeCode = "All"` and the replication is not yet complete for some emission data types, the `ReplicationLog` entries for `emissionDataTypeCode = "All"` will be added to the `ReplicationLog` for all remaining emission data types that are still in progress. ## Read Operations You can use the read-only operation `EmissionDataReplication` to retrieve the available replications. You have read-only operations that include navigations to the `FootprintInventoryScope` and `OverallStatusCode`. In addition, you have read-only operations for `FootprintInventoryScope`, `EmissionDataTypeCode`, `LogLevelCode`, `OverallStatusCode`, `PeriodicityCode`, `GHGScopeCode`, `GHGCategoryCode`, and code values are offered.

apis.Name: ItemFootprintsAPI
apis.Title: Item Footprints - V1
apis.ShortText: Retrieves the item footprints for analytics.
apis.Description:
# General This API is deprecated. We recommend that you use Item Footprint - V2 API.
The API lets you access calculated item footprint data for in-depth analysis. Use the analytics results to evaluate, analyze, and optimize resources to reduce footprints. ## Item Footprints The API retrieves key information, such as the Total Footprint and Footprint per Unit, for various items like Product, Energy Source, and Facility over a defined period. This enables you to efficiently evaluate environmental impacts for all the impact categories. Additionally, it provides details of the physical quantities, amounts, and units of measure used in the calculations. ## Item Footprint Transactions The API provides comprehensive details on various input and output transactions related to Product, Resource, and Energy footprints over a defined period. It also retrieves details about business transaction types, consumption quantities, amounts, impact categories, and units of measure used in the calculations. ## Item Footprint Breakdown The API provides comprehensive details about item footprint breakdown for a specific impact category over a defined period. It also retrieves details about impact categories, cost centers, footprint breakdown components, and units of measure used in the calculations. Item types, such as Business Activity and Waste Generated in Operations, are associated with locations. If cost centers are assigned to these locations, the API retrieves the ID of the assigned cost center. ## Item Footprint Transaction Breakdown The API provides comprehensive details about item footprint transaction breakdown for specific impact categories over a defined period. It retrieves details about input and output transactions related to product footprints, including business transaction types, consumption quantities, amounts, and units of measure used in the calculations. The API offers a granular breakdown of the footprint components within each impact category. It specifies the amounts and units of measure for each component.

apis.Name: SfmPeriodicDataAPIV2
apis.Title: Import Business Transactions (Corporate and Products)
apis.ShortText: Imports business transactions for footprint calculations.
apis.Description:
# General
   Imports the business transaction data (periodic data) from your source system and stores it in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management.
   Both the periodicity (monthly or yearly), the actual period, and the set of companies must be specified. 
## Entity Overview
 For all business transaction entities, the aggregated quantities can be imported to the solution. All of these entities have a **unique semantic key**

 - Plant
 - Service Product or Material
 - Possibly additional master data, depending on the transaction type
 - The Unit of Measure (UoM)

 By convention, **all quantities** have **positive values**. Note that most transaction types have a "mirror" or contrary transaction type. Therefore, instead of negative values, for example, a GoodsReceiptFromSupplier, a GoodsReturnToSupplier would be present.


 Entities with missing or unknown references or code values, or with negative quantities, will be marked as inconsistent in the solution. The footprint calculation does not consider such inconsistent records.
 ## Lifecycle Actions

 To start the import of periodic data, an action `notifyOfStartOfReplication` is offered. The body of the request must contain `{ footprintInventoryScopeIdentifier: <scope identifier>, period: "<yyyy / yyyy-mm>" }`. The `period` should be in ISO format (`yyyy` for a yearly aggregation or `yyyy-mm` for a monthly aggregation). This action returns a `replicationId` which identifies the combination of scope (periodicity and set of companies) and period, and is required as an input for all other actions.

 To restart the replication for a specific periodic data entity, an action `notifyOfPartialRestartOfReplication` is offered. The body of the request must contain `{ replicationId: <replicationId>, periodicDataTypeCode: <entity name> }`. This action deletes all previous records of periodic data for this entity, scope and period.

 To restart the replication for all the periodic data entities for a specific replication ID, an action `notifyOfRestartOfReplication` is offered. The body of the request must contain `{ replicationId: <replicationId>}`. This action deletes all previous records of periodic data for the scope and period.


 After starting (or restarting) a replication, the actual data is replicated to the solution using the Data Import Operations described in the corresponding section below.

 As soon as the source ERP system finishes replicating a periodic data entity type, it calls `notifyOfEndOfReplication` to document the completion of the replication of this type. Note that replication of all instances and log messages for a periodic data type must have been completed before calling the operation. The body of the request must contain `{ replicationId: <replicationId>, periodicDataTypeCode: <entity name> }`. The value `"All"` as an `entity name` allows to set all not-yet-completed entities to completed in one call. This may be useful in cases where a source ERP system does not support all entity types and does not transfer any data for the remaining entity types.

  ## Read Services

 To identify the available `PeriodicDataReplication`, a read-only service is offered which returns the available replications, including a navigation to the `FootprintInventoryScope`.
 In addition, read-only services for `FootprintInventoryScope` and code values are offered.

 ## Data Import Operations

 For the actual data import, mass insert actions are offered. As master data supports both an initial load or creation and delta updates, the related API for master data is a mass _upsert_. On the other hand, periodic data is only created once per period (usually after the period is closed and immutable). Hence, PeriodicData can only be _inserted_, and sending data twice for the same key is not supported.

 Besides the periodic data entities themselves, error logs can be created by `massInsertReplicationLog`. Supported values for `logLevelCode` are I (info), W (warning), E (error), and S (success).

 The ReplicationLog can also be created for `periodicDataTypeCode = "All"`. This can be used to indicate errors that cannot be attributed to a specific entity.
   If `ReplicationLog` with `logLevelCode = "E"` is created, the replication will end with the status `Aborted`.

   In case the `notifyOfEndOfReplication` is called for `masterDataTypeCode = "All"` and the replication is not yet complete for some entities, the ReplicationLog entries for `masterDataTypeCode = "All"` will be added to the ReplicationLog for all remaining entities that are still in progress.

apis.Name: sap-bdc-dus-PotentialCustomerProfile-v1
apis.Title: Potential Customer Profile
apis.ShortText: Provides harmonized customer profile data, consolidating information from multiple source systems through advanced identity resolution and unification processes.
apis.Description:
The Potential Customer Profile data product is the harmonized output generated by the SAP Datasphere, data composer, providing a single trusted profile view of each customer based on disparate records coming into the data composer from multiple sources. This data product can be consumed by other systems to improve analytics, personalization, and operational efficiency across the organization.

**Business Context**: Each customer profile in this data product contains attribute data for that customer, such as first and last name, email address, physical address, and so on. The list of potential attributes is predefined for the data product, and which specific attributes will appear for any given profile will depend on the source data coming into the data composer, as well as the configuration of the data composer.

apis.Name: ScreeningV2
apis.Title: Screening (Version 2)
apis.ShortText: Screen business partners' names and addresses against sanctioned party lists, producing screening hits for possible matches.
apis.Description:
To screen business partners of a single business object, you must POST resource /screeningRequests of the Screening API. Most requests will pass through without any hits, which is indicated by _result_ `N` in the response. For these cases, you can continue your business process immediately without any follow-up actions. Some screening requests will indicate that there are potential hits by responding with _result_ `P`. These requests will produce Screened Objects that must then be decided by actual end-users. Use the key of the posted screeningRequest to poll the ScreeningHits API. Potential hits that already have a decision in ScreeningHits can influence the _result_ of the screening request. Responses with _result_ `C` indicate that at least one potential hit has already been confirmed. If all potential hits already have been rejected, the _result_ will be `N`.
To screen multiple business partners directly, you must POST resource /multipleScreeningRequests with unique business object ids.

apis.Name: SCIMService
apis.Title: User Management (SCIM) for Procurement Planning
apis.ShortText: Writes and reads user data
apis.Description:
Read and write user data that can then be used by the Identity Provisioning Service. The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Service is protected by the Identity Authentication Service, which means you need to configure the authentication in the Identity Provisioning Service. You can use this service to replicate users into SAP Ariba Procurement Planning. To find users in the list of available users when, for example, adding team members to a project or starting a workflow, these users first have to be replicated using this service.
## Rate Limitations
For more information about the API rate and size limits for SAP Ariba Procurement Planning, see [API Rate and Size Limits](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_PROCUREMENT_PLANNING/fe81d41276694c218ab0f6e3f78cfad3/39b42e0e51054ed5ad5b886afecb7f0e.html).

apis.Name: Watchlists
apis.Title: Watch List
apis.ShortText: Create and manage a custom watch list to screen for your own list of entities.
apis.Description: Use this API to manage the uploaded custom watch list to screen for your own list of entities. To create it, begin with POST /customWatchlistVersion for the first version. Fill the inactive version with entities by calling PUT /customWatchlistVersion/entities until you have supplied all data. When finished, activate the version for screening with POST /customWatchlistVersion/activate. GET /customWatchlist/info lets you check the latest active and inactive versions, including their capacity and activation state. If you made a mistake when creating or filling in your last custom watch list version, you can delete it with DELETE /customWatchlistVersion/{id}. When creating subsequent versions, you can keep the entities from the last version by using POST /customWatchlistVersion with upload type `DELTA`; you can then PUT /customWatchlistVersion/entities to supply only the entities that you'd like to change.

Import data within one import session (see **Service Operations** - **/Import{EntityName}**).\ This call can be made several times per import session.\ **Example:** If you want to import **_products_** and **_product groups_**, then you would have to call **_/ImportProducts_** and **_/ImportProductGroups_** within the same import session and then proceed with the next steps. 2. apis.Name: sap-s4com-ConsolidationVersion-v1
apis.Title: Consolidation Version
apis.ShortText: Data Product Consolidation Version
apis.Description:
A consolidation version is a distinct version of data in consolidation. In addition to a consolidation version for actual data, other versions of data that can be managed in parallel can be created, so that alternative results for the purposes of simulation, planning, and restatement can be produced. A consolidation version can be used for parallel processing with different data categories, accounting principles, and valuations, such as multiple group currencies.
To each consolidation version, special versions are assigned. The assignment of special versions enables the reuse of the maintained settings of a special version among different consolidation versions: The control parameters are entered only once in a special version and these settings are then reflected in all the consolidation versions to which the special version is assigned. Examples for special versions are data entry, consolidation unit attributes, financial statement item attributes, group structure, exchange rates, reclassification and elimination.

apis.Name: PSM_ISI_R_II_MAINTAIN_OBJ_ID_MAPPING_IN
apis.Title: Manage Object Identifier Mappings
apis.ShortText: The inbound maintain service OIM is a web-service interface for maintaining object-identifier mappings between objects in an SAP remote business system and a local SAP On-Demand system.
apis.Description:
The web-service interface **Maintain Object Identifier Mapping In** enables you to connect external applications to your SAP On-Demand system and to maintain (create, update, or delete) object-identifier mappings between object identifiers in a remote business system, such as an SAP ERP or a SAP CRM suite system and object identifiers in the SAP On-Demand system.

The **Maintain Object Identifier Mapping In** web-service interface offers two operations, MAINTAIN_BUNDLE and CHECK_MAINTAIN_BUNDLE.

The web-service interface uses a remote object ID with its remote ID type and a local object ID with its local ID type. Remote objects are objects located in a business system. Local objects are objects located in an SAP On-Demand system.

A Web service handles an application-specific business document. "Business documents" used in the following descriptions are object-identifier mappings when dealing with the **Maintain Object Identifier Mapping In** web-service interface.

apis.Name: PSM_ISI_R_II_FIA_ACC_WIP
apis.Title: Work In Process Clearing Run Create
apis.ShortText: An interface to create and execute Work-in-Process (WIP) Clearing Run instance.
apis.Description:
Work-in-process (WIP) clearing runs are periodic tasks that are usually performed at regularly scheduled times or during period closing to correct and clear the work in process account. A run selects all production lots that have the corresponding status and reduces the associated work-in-process inventory to zero.

By taking account of all changes to work in process during the period, WIP clearing runs ensure that the value of the work in process is correctly reported at the end of the period.

WIP clearing runs determine any remaining work in process balances for production lots that have the logistical status Finished. If any differences occurred for the production lots, the system applies the perpetual cost method (Standard or Moving Average) and zeroes out the balances. The resulting postings depend on the cost method. WIP clearing runs generate journal entries in the general ledger.

The Web service interface Accounting WIP Clearing Run enables you to create and execute Work-in-Process Clearing Run instance. This Web service interface Accounting WIP Clearing Run has operation Create WIP which enable user to create and execute WIP run instance.

This WIP run instance can be shown in UI under Inventory Valuation WorkCentre WIP Clearing work center view.

Here is an example of a simple Web service request
```
<n0:WIPCreateRequest xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global">
<WIPRun>
<ProductionLotID>31</ProductionLotID>
<RunDescription languageCode="EN">Run Description</RunDescription>
<AccountingPeriodID>010</AccountingPeriodID>
<FiscalYearID>2015</FiscalYearID>
<AccountingClosingStepCode>010</AccountingClosingStepCode>
<CompanyID>MC10000</CompanyID>
<SetOfBooksID schemeID="Token 7" schemeAgencyID="Token 8">01</SetOfBooksID>
<BusinessResidence>MC64000</BusinessResidence>
<TestRunIndicator>true</TestRunIndicator>
</WIPRun>
</n0:WIPCreateRequest>
```
 

Production lot ID defines the production lot "31" on which the run will be performed.

Run Description provides the description of WIP run which can help to find run instance in UI under Inventory Valuation work center WIP Clearing work center view.

Accounting period value ‘010’ selects all production lot which are finished in this accounting period.

Fiscal year value ‘2015’ provides fiscal year to post journal entry. Accounting closing steps value posts journal entry with closing steps ‘010’.

Set of books defines the set of books where the journal entries are posted by the WIP Run.

If the Test run indicator value is selected to be ‘true’, WIP run will be created in test mode (simulation) which will not create any journal entry.

Here is an example of a simple Web service response.
```
<n0:WIPRunResponse xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global" xmlns:prx="urn:sap.com:proxy:QCL:/1SAI/TAS321CE61824281D1B131F:804">
<WIPResponse>
<WIPRunStatus>true</WIPRunStatus>
</WIPResponse>
</n0:WIPRunResponse>
```
 

Here WIP run status ‘true’ means WIP run instance create successfully. This run instance can be found in UI Inventory Valuation work center WIP Clearing work center view.

Run instance can also be found using ‘run description’ provided in request parameter while creating run. In case there is any error then response parameter <WIPRunStatus> value would be false to indicate that there is not any instance created for WIP.

```
<n0:CalculatePricesRequest_sync xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global">

```
 

**Note: for the above request with extension field to work, Price Master data should be in place for given extension field in system**

Note: Incase, if for a given account ID MC9785 ,if there are no price master data existing (Customer specific Price) for a given product, then the most relevant price(Base price) of the product is selected.

It would extract most relevant price (in this case base price, since no other key except product id is passed to service) for 1 ea of material MCF-0001.

Note: Incase, if more than one key is passed AccountID , SalesOrganisationID + DistributionChannel

Case 1: In the ByDesign system Customer specific and Sales Organisation specific prices are maintained for the given product, then most relevant price is picked , in this case Customer specific price is picked.

Case 2: in ByDesign system Customer specific price for given product is not maintained , but Sales Organisation specific prices are maintained for the given product, then most relevant price is picked , in this case Sales Organisation price is picked.

Case 3: in ByDesign system Customer specific price and Sales Organisation specific for given product is not maintained ,then most relevant price is picked , in this case Base price is picked.

__Service works for Extension fields at Header/General and Item level__ -> for more details refer to Help Center documentation for topic 'Pricing with Extension Fields'

apis.Name: PSM_ISI_R_II_SLO_SO_BUNDLE_MBO
apis.Title: Manage Sales Orders
apis.ShortText: An interface to replicate or create sales orders from a source system or file, to a target system.
apis.Description:
This web-service is used to create or modify existing sales orders.

It consists of the **MaintainBundle** and the **CheckMaintainBundle** operations. **MaintainBundle** is used to create or update one or more instances of the sales order. **CheckMaintainBundle** is used to check if one or more instances of the sales order can be maintained.

apis.Name: PSM_ISI_R_II_PRC_SPL_MANAGE_IN
apis.Title: Manage Sales Price Lists High Volume
apis.ShortText: An interface to create or update sales price list and sales discount list from a source system or file.
apis.Description:
The Web service interface **Manage Sales Price List In** enables you to connect external applications to your SAP Business ByDesign system and to create and edit sales price list and sales discount list in your system.

The term "sales price list" will be used in this documentation to refer to both sales price list and sales discount list.

The Web service interface **Manage Sales Price List In** offers the operations **Maintain Bundle** and **Check Maintain Bundle**.

Here is an example of a simple Web service request:
```
<n0:SalesPriceListBundleMaintainRequest_sync xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global">
 <BasicMessageHeader>
 <ID>MSG1</ID>
 </BasicMessageHeader>
 <SalesPriceList ActionCode="01">
 <ObjectNodeSenderTechnicalID>TECHID1</ObjectNodeSenderTechnicalID>
 <TypeCode>7PL0</TypeCode>
 <ID>SPLID1</ID>
 <Description languageCode="EN">Customer Group Specific Price List 
 </Description>
 <StartDate>2013-01-01</StartDate>
 <EndDate>2013-12-31</EndDate>
 <CurrencyCode>EUR</CurrencyCode>
 <SalesOrgID>MC42200</SalesOrgID>
 <DistributionChannelCode>01</DistributionChannelCode>
 <CustomerGroupCode>02</CustomerGroupCode>
 <PriceSpecification>
 <TypeCode>7PR1</TypeCode>
 <Amount currencyCode="EUR">200.00</Amount>
 <BaseQuantity unitCode="EA">1</BaseQuantity>
 <BaseQuantityTypeCode>EA</BaseQuantityTypeCode>
 <ProductID>MCA-0001</ProductID>
 <ProductTypeCode>1</ProductTypeCode>
 </PriceSpecification>
 </SalesPriceList>
</n0:SalesPriceListBundleMaintainRequest_sync>
```
 

It would create a single price list with ID SPLID1 and currency EUR valid throughout 2013 for a certain combination of sales organization, distribution chnannel and customer group containing a single price of 200 EUR for 1 ea of material MCA-0001.

apis.ShortText: An interface to read the data of selected fields of a supplier invoice or to maintain one or more supplier invoices.
apis.Description:
The **Manage Supplier Invoice In** inbound service interface contains an operation that reads the data of selected fields of a supplier invoice and prepares this data for a specific data consumer.

The inbound service interface enables you to create one or more supplier invoices and to read data of selected fields of a supplier invoice.

This interface is relevant if your company wants to read the data of selected fields of a supplier invoice or to upload one or more supplier invoices from external applications.

The **Manage Supplier Invoice In** interface offers the operations **Check_Maintain_Bundle**, **Maintain_Bundle** and **Read_SI**

You can create invoicing documents such as invoices with or without reference, customs invoices, credit memos, and down payment requests in the invoice entry view of the supplier invoicing work center.

Note: In this document, supplier invoice is used as a superordinate term for an invoice, credit memo, down payment request, and customs invoice.

Here is an example of a simple web service request to read a supplier invoice:

</n0:SupplierInvoiceByIDQuery_sync>

apis.Title: Manage Employee Time Accounts Adjustments
apis.ShortText: An interface to maintain the employee time acount adjustments for a posting date.
apis.Description:
The web service interface "Manage Employee Time Accounts Custom Adjustments in" enables you to make programmatic adjustments to the quantities against the time accounts that are assigned to various employees.

Typically, quota time accounts like Vacation have accrual rules that can be set up in business configuration. However, there may be customer specific / country specific accrual or entitlement conditions that cannot be met using the standard options available. This web service allows you to connect an external application that performs this accrual / entitlement quantity calculation, and updates the employee time account data with the calculated quantity. This external application may also be a Cloud Studio application.

The web service interface offers the operations MaintainBundle.

here is an example.
```

 <EmployeeID>EmployeeID</EmployeeID>
 <PostingDate>2015-03-01</PostingDate>
 <TimeAccountTypeCode>Time Account</TimeAccountTypeCode>
 <Quantity unitCode ='Unit'>27</Quantity>
 <QuantityTypeCode>TIME</QuantityTypeCode>
 <TimeAccountPostingTypeCode></TimeAccountPostingTypeCode>

 </EmployeeTimeAccountCustomAdjustments>
</n0:EmployeeTimeAccountsCustomAdjustmentBundleMaintainRequest_sync>

```
